name: How do you price an in-law suite when the design is custom and luxury finishes are involved?

mainEntity.name: How do you price an in-law suite when the design is custom and luxury finishes are involved?
mainEntity.text: How do you price an in-law suite when the design is custom and luxury finishes are involved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Custom and luxury in-law suites should be priced with a line-item approach, because premium finishes can change the budget dramatically. Start with the structural and code-required baseline, then add finish upgrades such as custom cabinetry, designer tile, high-end appliances, premium windows, integrated lighting, and upgraded flooring. Site work, utility extensions, and engineering should be priced separately from aesthetic choices. That makes it easier to decide where to spend and where to save. For luxury projects in areas like Beverly Hills, West Hollywood, Pasadena, or Santa Monica, the finish level often matters as much as the layout itself. A clear estimate helps homeowners understand whether they are building a functional suite or a custom guest residence.
acceptedAnswer.description: Luxury in-law suites are priced by scope, not just square footage. Custom cabinetry, premium fixtures, high-end windows, structural changes, and complex site work can push costs up quickly. A detailed estimate should separate base construction from finish upgrades so homeowners can compare options clearly.
